chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Abdillah ibn Jabalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one in Ihram who plucks the hair from his armpit, he said: He must feed three poor people.

The correct interpretation of this report is that we apply it to the one who plucked from one armpit, because the first [part of the report] is directed toward the one who plucked from both armpits entirely, so a sheep's blood [expiation] became obligatory for him.

key_terms.مُحرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for plucking armpit hair while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to clarify the scope of expiation (kaffarah) for plucking armpit hair during Ihram. The scholar employs the principle of contextual inference (qiyas al-awlawiyyah) to distinguish between the specific case of plucking one armpit, which requires feeding three poor people, and the more severe case of placking both, which incurs the blood of a sheep.
